question: Which sweetener, first used in 1879, has received FDA approval for use in fruit juice beverages?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Saccharin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Saccharin** was discovered in 1879 by chemists Constantin Fahlberg and Ira Remsen.
 
• It is one of the oldest artificial sweeteners and has been widely used in food and beverages.
 
• The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved saccharin for use in fruit juice beverages and other food products.
 
• Saccharin is calorie-free and approximately **200–700 times sweeter than sugar**, making it a popular choice for low-calorie diets.
 
• It is commonly used in diet sodas, chewing gums, and other sugar-free products as a sweetening agent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Artificial Sweeteners:** These are chemical or natural compounds used to sweeten food and beverages without the calories of sugar.
 
• **FDA Approval Process:** The FDA evaluates artificial sweeteners for safety through rigorous testing before approving their use in food products.
 
• **Other Popular Artificial Sweeteners:** Aspartame, sucralose, and neotame are other FDA-approved sweeteners used in various foods and drinks.
 
• **Health Concerns:** While saccharin was once linked to cancer risk, subsequent studies and regulatory reviews concluded that it is safe for consumption.
 
• **Calorie-Free Benefits:** Artificial sweeteners like saccharin are helpful for individuals managing diabetes or following low-calorie diets.
